source.title: SGD as Free Energy Minimization: A Thermodynamic View on Neural Network Training
source.authors: Ildus Sadrtdinov; Ivan Klimov; E. Lobacheva; D. Vetrov

record.file_problem: none; full paper text supplied, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Reports its own CIFAR network training results on training loss and convergence across learning rates and parameterization regimes. The training setup and measures differ from the claim versions’ main benchmarks or interventions, but directly test whether the reported models converge or remain at nonzero training loss.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s own CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 results on training loss and convergence. The free-energy temperature estimates, SNR measurements, and cited results are not separate rows for the claim unless they report the training behavior named by a version. The study does not test random-label fitting, shortcut removal, initialization comparisons, learning rates above a stability threshold, or batch-normalization speed.
record.test_reason: The study measures stationary training loss, weight entropy and gradient dynamics, but does not report zero or near-zero training classification error as required by V1. Convergence toward an unspecified minimum does not establish that result. It also does not test the interventions or stability-threshold dynamics named by V2–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that their experiments support a free-energy description of fixed-rate SGD, balancing training loss against weight-distribution entropy. Estimated temperature increases with learning rate in stationary regimes and decays toward zero during low-rate training of nominally OP models. They attribute the contrast to stochastic-gradient behavior near minima. Their empirical qualification matters: the baseline OP CIFAR-10 ConvNet does not exhibit the gradient-decay behavior required by their strict theoretical OP definition, and its eventual asymptotic behavior remains unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: Uses projected SGD on fully scale-invariant networks with fixed learning rates and independent batch sampling; studies stationary loss and entropy and SNR rather than training classification error, random labels, or the claim versions’ interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome depends on parameterization regime and learning rate: UP models stabilize; OP models converge at low learning rates but stabilize at moderate learning rates. The paper excludes runs that have not stabilized or are in high-rate divergence regimes from temperature estimation.

fits_no_version.finding: Fixed-rate projected SGD produces learning-rate-dependent loss plateaus; nominally overparameterized models instead show continuing loss decreases at sufficiently small rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In fully scale-invariant CIFAR networks constrained to the unit sphere, stationary loss and convergence behavior depend on learning rate and parameterization.

fits_no_version.finding: The nominally OP CIFAR-10 ConvNet has a stochastic-versus-full-gradient decay exponent of approximately 0.78; smaller datasets move the exponent toward 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Greater overparameterization makes stochastic and full gradient decay rates more similar in the tested networks.

fits_no_version.finding: The spherical toy problem reaches loss below 10^-16 in its interpolating configuration, while its noninterpolating configuration fluctuates above the minimum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interpolation changes fixed-rate projected-SGD convergence in the constructed spherical optimization problem.

record.problems: The paper reports training loss and convergence but not training classification error, so the zero-error behavior central to V1 cannot be directly determined. The entropy estimate is non-parametric and may be biased in high-dimensional weight spaces, as the authors acknowledge. The results use projected SGD and fixed scale-invariant weights, not ordinary unconstrained training.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, including random or corrupted labels; substantial classification error under smaller-model, early-stopping or regularized conditions. No training classification-error results are reported.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious local-minimum frequencies and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth, matched identity-shortcut comparisons and the stated initialization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons, signal preservation, training speed and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to the initial linearized stability limit, loss-rise recovery with curvature reduction, and full-batch sharpness tracking the stability threshold.
Matched normalization comparisons for training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Section 4 describes convergence as requiring 100% training accuracy, but supplies no measured accuracy result for these runs. That regime description does not turn decreasing-loss observations into demonstrated zero classification error. Nonzero loss likewise need not imply classification mistakes. No verdict follows from missing classification-error measurements. High-rate divergence is not a V5 test without the specified stability-threshold and curvature measurements.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report corrupted or random-label training; does not compare SGD with Adam; does not establish the stated smaller-model, early-stopping, or regularized-recipe results.

rows.subject: ConvNet
rows.operation_detail: Projected SGD with fixed learning rate and batch size; training loss reported across learning rates.
rows.measure: Training loss and its behavior over iterations across learning rates
rows.value: Training loss stabilizes by the end of training except for the smallest learning rates, which require more iterations to reach stationarity; stationary training loss increases monotonically with learning rate.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviation for loss is computed over several iterations of the same training run; numerical values not stated in text.
rows.note: The paper describes stationary loss behavior but does not state that training classification error reaches zero; the smallest learning rates have not yet stabilized within the reported run.
rows.check: Stationary training loss does not establish substantial training classification error in the smaller model. The reported plateau cannot be classified as partial V1.

rows.subject: ConvNet
rows.operation_detail: Projected SGD with fixed learning rate and batch size; training loss reported across learning rates.
rows.measure: Training loss and its behavior over iterations across learning rates
rows.value: For moderate learning rates, training loss stabilizes over iterations; both loss and entropy increase with learning rate.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviation for loss is computed over several iterations of the same training run; numerical values not stated in text.
rows.note: The cited passage gives no numerical training classification error and does not say that stationary training loss is zero.
rows.check: A nonzero stationary loss at moderate learning rates does not establish nonzero training classification error.

rows.subject: ConvNet

conditions.value: low; exact values not stated in the passage

rows.value: The model converges to an optimum, with a consistent decrease in loss and entropy; metrics do not stabilize within a reasonable number of iterations.
rows.note: Convergence is reported, but the passage does not give training classification error or say the loss is zero.
rows.check: Decreasing loss and reported convergence toward an optimum do not establish zero or near-zero training classification error. The metrics remain unstabilized during the observed run.
